advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add a guard in suppress_and_dedup that passes through findings already carrying a drop_reason, or remove that claim from the docstring.
evidence: Docstring: 'Findings already carrying a ``drop_reason`` are left untouched (a prior stage owns them).' (decide.py:267-268)

Loop body decide.py:274-283 iterates every finding unconditionally: `for f in findings: if is_contentless_finding(f): ... key = dedup_key(f); if key in seen: ...` — no `if f.get('drop_reason'): kept.append(f); continue` guard.
Harmless today because the only caller passes freshly-decided `discovered` (orchestrator.py:456) with no drop_reason, but the false contract will mislead reuse.
advisory.finding: suppress_and_dedup's docstring states 'Findings already carrying a drop_reason are left untouched (a prior stage owns them)' but the implementation has no guard for a pre-existing drop_reason — it will run is_contentless_finding/dedup and potentially re-stamp such a finding, contradicting the documented contract.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add at the top of the loop: `if f.get("drop_reason"): kept.append(f); continue` — or delete the 'left untouched' sentence from the docstring to match behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] When collapsing duplicates, keep the highest-severity decision (block > advisory > indeterminate) as the surviving representative rather than blindly the first occurrence.
evidence: suppress_and_dedup keeps the first-seen key and drops later ones: decide.py:278-283, with no tie-break on decision severity.
Discovered order prepends DET blocks then DET advisories then LLM findings (orchestrator.py:416-445), so an advisory can be the kept representative of a later block.
This contradicts the change's stated intent that a duplicate BLOCK must not fail to reach the blocking bucket (orchestrator.py:449-451).
advisory.finding: suppress_and_dedup keeps the first occurrence of a duplicate group regardless of decision severity; since DET-advisory and earlier advisory findings precede later findings in the discovered order, an LLM 'block' that exactly duplicates an earlier 'advisory' (same criteria set + location + normalized body) is dropped as 'duplicate', silently retaining only the weaker advisory and losing the block.
advisory.suggested_fix: In suppress_and_dedup, when a duplicate key is seen, compare decisions and promote the kept finding to 'block' (or swap representatives) if the incoming duplicate outranks it, instead of unconditionally dropping the later one.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a suppress_and_dedup test where the duplicate pair has equal criteria sets in different order (e.g. ["E2","P1"] vs ["P1","E2"]) and assert they collapse to one.
evidence: decide.py:256 `criteria = tuple(sorted(_norm_text(c) for c in (f.get("criteria") or []) if _norm_text(c)))`
Duplicate-pair fixture uses identical `"criteria": ["E2"]` on both members (test_plan_review.py:924,935) — no test varies criteria order.
ABSENCE: no test constructs two findings with equal criteria SETS but different list order to assert they dedup.
advisory.finding: dedup_key's documented order-insensitivity of criteria (the sorted() in the key) is untested: every dedup test uses identical single-element criteria ['E2'], so removing the sort() would still pass all tests. A duplicate pair whose criteria lists differ only in order would silently fail to collapse without any test catching it.
scenarios: Two finders emit the same finding with criteria ["E2","P1"] vs ["P1","E2"]; a refactor dropping sorted() stops deduping them.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a finding whose body is under 'detail' (empty vs non-empty) is correctly classified contentless/deduped via finding_body's fallback keys.
evidence: docstring decide.py:216-220 names the `ReviewResult` finding schema keying the body `detail`.
ABSENCE: every fixture/finding in the new tests uses `"finding": ...`; none uses `detail`/`body`/`description`, so the fallback branch of finding_body is never exercised.
docstring decide.py:267-268 `Findings already carrying a ``drop_reason`` are left untouched (a prior stage owns them).`
decide.py:274-283: the loop has no `if f.get("drop_reason")` guard; every finding is checked.
ABSENCE: no test passes a finding with a preset drop_reason (e.g. 'novelty'/'completion') through suppress_and_dedup to assert it is passed through unchanged.
advisory.finding: finding_body's documented fallback body keys ('detail'/'body'/'description', the ReviewResult finding shape) are untested: all tests key the body as 'finding' only. Contentless detection and dedup over a 'detail'-keyed finding — an explicitly supported live shape — has no regression coverage.
merged_from: The suppress_and_dedup contract 'findings already carrying a drop_reason are left untouched (a prior stage owns them)' is neither implemented nor tested — the loop unconditionally runs is_contentless_finding/dedup on every finding. No test feeds a pre-dropped finding through to assert its reason is preserved rather than being re-stamped/re-narrowed.
scenarios: A ReviewResult-shaped finding (body under 'detail') is contentless or a duplicate; if the fallback key ordering breaks it is not caught.
